# Phyllum

> A design system companion that turns prose, images, or the styles already in a codebase into named tokens and components, all recorded in one file.

Phyllum writes exactly one file in a user's codebase: `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`, plus a
`DESIGN-SYSTEM.md.bak` holding the state one edit ago, plus its own gitignored
`.phyllum/` — and, only when you name one on the command line, the `.json` file
`assess --json` writes. From v0.5.0 `apply` writes one line back into
`DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` with no question asked — the `applied:` line of each
component's spec block and nothing else in the file — a derived reading of
whether the codebase is using that component right now; the amendment is
recorded in `skill/refs/apply/apply.md` and in SKILL.md's permission table
rather than left to be discovered. Every command is rerunnable and converges — re-assessing doesn't
duplicate tokens, re-creating a component opens a revision. `assess` reads the codebase,
`tokenise` reads a sentence, `create` reads intent, and `apply` plans getting the recorded
system into the code — writing a reviewable PRD to `.phyllum/PRD.md` and executing none of
it — and `update` is the editing verb, changing a token or component the design system
already records, and `delete` is the removal verb, taking one recorded component away behind a breaking-change warning, an in-use block and two confirmations; moving the install is `upgrade`. `apply run` is the single exception to the write rule: it executes that plan on a
`phyllum/apply-<date>` branch of its own, one commit per phase, writing only the files the
running phase's criteria name. Mechanical commands run in pure Node; the intelligent ones
(`create`, `tokenise`) run natively inside a Claude Code session or shell out to the
`claude` CLI — with one exception inside `create`: `create primitives` is wholly
mechanical, shipped constants and deterministic arithmetic, so it needs no model.
Phyllum's naming vocabulary and its ramp constants are shipped as parsed spec tables in
`skill/refs/`, never as code and never as an npm dependency; the zero-dependency rule is
absolute.
These paths are repo-relative. Phyllum is published on npm as `phyllum`; the source lives at https://github.com/ndisisnd/phyllum.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what Phyllum is, how to install it, how it works
- [Skill definition](skill/SKILL.md): the router — commands, the file format, the two rules that outrank being helpful. Start here to change behaviour.
- [CLI entry point](bin/phyllum.js): argument parsing and the single call into execute; the terminal surface
- [File template](templates/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md): the canonical DESIGN-SYSTEM.md skeleton every install scaffolds

## Reference

Every protocol's reference is a folder of per-topic files (v0.4.1); the file named after the protocol is the frame and everything else is a topic, so a session loads the one file the moment needs. `nomenclature.md` is the one flat file — a shared library, loaded whole.

- [create](skill/refs/create/): the three modes (prose, image, pick), the fifteen archetype contracts, custom mode — no contract, no gap list, recorded exactly as described and marked as such — the follow-up loop, acceptance and the write step, plus `create primitives` — primitive colour ramps, asked per token, written under Colours' `Primitives` subsection
- [assess](skill/refs/assess/): the read-only codebase scan — what is read (text files in any language, bounded: build output, dependency directories, gitignored paths, oversized files and non-text files are skipped), React-only component detection, clustering before naming, the diff on rerun, and the judgement half: severities on every finding, similarity groups scored into clone/similar bands, naming drift and prop mismatches, hygiene (framework collisions, unused tokens and components), and the drift score and verdict the run ends in; `--json [path]` writes the whole assessment to one file instead of reviewing it
- [apply](skill/refs/apply/): planning the design system into the code and then executing that plan — harness detection and its precedence, one acceptance criterion per change, one phase per commit, the PRD's marker contract, resume vs `--fresh`, and for `apply run`: the harness hand-off, the branch and commit guarantees, the mechanical-vs-agent split, `.phyllum/config.json`'s model overrides, per-phase verification, the source-write grant, and — from v0.5.0 — the `applied` flag: what each reading means, the `alreadyAdopted` evidence it is derived from, derived-never-declared, the flip table (every `apply` run, a committed adopt phase, a harness hand-off, any other command that rewrites a spec block), and the tolerance that lets a file with no flag read exactly as it did
- [tokenise](skill/refs/tokenise/): naming the values in one sentence — the proposal queue and its splitting grammar (several values in one sentence, one question at a time, in sentence order, duplicates collapsed, a skip costing only itself), the three passes, every colour format read alike (`#2563EB`, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`, `hsl()`, `#rrggbbaa`) with values compared by channel — alpha included, so two alphas are two facts — and recorded exactly as typed, gradients as a colour value (the six `*-gradient()` shapes, recorded verbatim, written into Colours, every proposed name carrying the word `gradient` and `gradient-{n}` as the fallback scale), the kind picker an empty run opens (colour / typography / border radius / spacing / something else, with the solid-or-gradient fork under colour and the prose each pick builds), the argument hint every value question wears, the naming sources (the nomenclature library first where the sentence signals a role, the lightness/saturation scales as fallback), the follow-up loop, acceptance
- [init](skill/refs/init/init.md): the guided setup walkthrough — scaffold, skill install, optional seeding
- [nomenclature](skill/refs/nomenclature.md): the shared library no command owns — the standard token-naming vocabulary (four slots in a fixed order, a strict word list per slot: families, ranks, exception words, state words), the nine shipped neutral-ramp constants, and the fixed lightness-and-saturation scale a derived ramp is placed on. Read by `tokenise`'s name suggestions and by `create primitives`; it is data, not behaviour, and nothing in it runs on its own
- [gui](skill/refs/gui/): the localhost server contract and the three-view dashboard, plus the presentation contract — colour tokens as cards in a responsive grid (a rounded swatch on top, the name and then the value beneath it), near-white swatches bordered, gradients painted as the swatch fill and only a value the page recognises ever inlined into a style attribute, primitives ramps keeping their nine-step strips, typography as live specimens, and number tokens no longer under one "Numbers" umbrella (v0.6.0) — each distinct `applies to` reading in the file is its own first-class section, verbatim label, file order, a trailing `other` for blanks, a recognised reading drawing its values as a **specimen** (a radius tile, a spacing gap, a shadow card) captioned with the name and mono value, an unrecognised one falling back to the plain name-and-value line — laid out with documentation anatomy: a constrained `--measure` column, three heading tiers, a one-line `section__note` under every heading, spacing that separates sections more than it separates the rows inside one, and a sticky "On this page" rail tracking the sections as they scroll — and the Library panel's rendered component preview — a spec-projection rather than the stored code run in the page, one element per archetype from the preview-element column of `refs/create/archetypes.md`, every value through the widened shape gate, token names resolved against the tokens `/system` already carries, a `TODO` or unresolvable slot listed as an unrendered slot rather than guessed, plus the variant toggle over entries sharing a base name, the states toggle whose slots overlay the base, and the attribute controls for recorded icon slots — leading and trailing only, derived from the spec and never invented, drawn as a filled dot in the muted ink, projection-only; the page is drawn **light-first** (v0.7.0), a neutral near-white canvas under white 1px-bordered panels with near-black ink and an accent darkened to clear small-text contrast, dark the second reading of the same palette rather than the default, every rendered token, ramp, specimen and preview verified viewable on the light surface; every panel, Library section and grouped list shares one **container** idiom (border, radius, `--layer` fill), every count and the `applied` badge share one **chip** idiom, and the stylesheet defines a solid `.btn--primary` and a transparent `.btn--ghost`; the Backlog panel is cut by component (v0.7.0) — one container per component parsed from each line's trailing parenthetical, a trailing `other` container for lines that name none, a total-count chip in the panel header — and carries an **Assess** button that posts the prompt `assess` to `POST /prompt` for the terminal session to run, giving "Queued…" button feedback and never executing anything itself; hand-written styling (rounded on a two-step radius scale, hairline borders, Geist-first type stack) with no dependency, no webfont and no network fetch, the light · dark · system theme control persisted in `localStorage` and applied before first paint, read-only as ever
- [display](skill/refs/system/system.md): the terminal listing format, including each component's `applied` / `not applied` reading where its spec block records one and nothing at all where it does not; `system` is the same command under its older name, kept as a permanent alias
- [version](skill/refs/version/version.md): the installed version, the on-demand npm registry check, what happens offline, and a third row (v0.7.1) comparing the skill copy in the current directory against this install byte-for-byte — `in step`, a neutral `N of 46 files differ`, or `none in this directory`, an extra file counting as a difference, never "behind" or "out of date", no version stamp written
- [upgrade](skill/refs/upgrade/upgrade.md): moving the install to the latest published version — install detection (npm/pnpm, global/project), the graceful refusals, the skill re-sync, and a prune step (v0.7.1) that lists every file this version no longer ships, asks once, and removes only on a yes, bounded to `.claude/skills/phyllum/`
- [update](skill/refs/update/): the editing verb from v0.4.0 — the menu and its one 0.4.x `apply` breadcrumb, the `component`/`token` chains, prose target-matching (exact names resolve, anything else is asked about rather than guessed), the token flow (type → the full list of that section → pick → a sentence), the rename ripple over every spec slot and Backlog line, the convergence re-check on a new value, `update component` riding `create`'s own revision machinery, and the never-list: no codebase, no PRD, nothing written before the gate, no invented or corrected value, no deletion — removal is `delete`, below. It stopped being `apply`'s alias in v0.4.0, and `apply` carries no alias at all now
- [delete](skill/refs/delete/): the removal verb from v0.5.0 — one recorded component per run, behind the loudest gate in the product. The list with each component's archetype and `applied` reading, the pick (`phyllum delete <name>` pre-answers it, an unknown name lists and asks), a breaking-change warning that always prints before any question about proceeding, the in-use block (the `applied: true` flag when there is one, a live adoption read of the codebase when there is none, and no flag or option past a refusal), the acceptance gate showing exactly what goes, and then a second confirmation requiring the component's name typed back — which `--yes` and a non-interactive run never satisfy. The write is the one funnel, `.bak` first, surgical: the entry and its Backlog lines, nothing else in the file. `delete token` is reserved and refused with its reason, and `.phyllum/PRD.md` is left for the next `phyllum apply` to reconcile
